notes: Long architectural refactor (939 entries) moving daemon identity from per-worktree to per-repo. Good exercise for summarizer: the motivation (measured resource waste) is as important as the implementation.

reference.title: Collapse daemon-per-worktree into one daemon per repo
reference.summary: Measured and then fixed a real resource problem: 12 ox daemons were holding 185MB of RAM across what should have been two repos, because daemon identity was keyed off worktree path. Three parallel explore agents mapped every per-worktree assumption across config, IPC, sync, and registry. The fix rekeyed daemon identity to SHA256(repo_id), added a graceful stopLegacyDaemon migration for existing users, and taught the daemon about multiple clones via CallerID/CallerPath tracking so ox status and ox agent list still show the right context. Landed as PR #181 with 3 commits and 17 new tests.
key_actions: Ran 3 parallel explore subagents to map per-worktree assumptions across config, IPC, sync, and registry
Measured live system footprint: 12 daemons, 185MB for 2 repos
Rekeyed daemon WorkspaceID from worktree path hash to repo_id hash
Added stopLegacyDaemon() migration to gracefully retire old path-based daemons
Added CallerID/CallerPath tracking so multi-clone users still get useful status
Improved ox status and ox agent list output for the shared-daemon world
Wrote 17 new tests covering identity, migration, and multi-caller flows
